Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Centre Manager & ECT
Job Title: Child Care Worker
Salary range: $79,500 - $86,600 - depending on skills level and work experience + superannuation.
Job Closure date: 30 days

About This Role:
Our client is a well-established early learning provider committed to nurturing children's growth through play-based learning and holistic development. With purpose-built facilities and a team of dedicated educators, they create warm, inclusive environments where children feel safe to explore, learn and thrive. Their philosophy emphasizes emotional wellbeing, creativity and foundational skill-building during these crucial early years.
We're seeking a nurturing Childcare Worker to join their team. This role goes beyond supervision - you'll actively contribute to children's developmental milestones while fostering their curiosity through engaging, age-appropriate experiences.

Key Duties & Responsibilities:
Program Delivery & Child Development:
• Design and implement stimulating educational programs aligned with the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF)
• Facilitate intentional teaching moments through play-based activities including storytelling, music, art and sensory exploration
• Observe and document children's progress to support individual learning goals and share insights with families
• Guide social-emotional development by modelling positive behaviour and conflict resolution strategies

Daily Care & Wellbeing:
• Maintain impeccable hygiene standards including nappy changing, toileting assistance and mealtime supervision
• Create predictable routines that provide children with emotional security while allowing flexibility for spontaneous learning
• Conduct thorough safety checks of indoor/outdoor environments and resources before activities
• Administer first aid when required and follow health management plans for children with additional needs

Family & Community Engagement:
• Build trusting relationships with families through daily conversations and formal progress updates
• Collaborate with room leaders to create displays that make children's learning visible to parents
• Participate in community events and centre initiatives that strengthen family connections

Compliance & Professionalism:
• Maintain current working with children check - first aid certification and relevant qualifications
• Contribute to quality improvement processes through reflective practice
• Attend staff meetings and professional development sessions to enhance practice

Skills & Requirements:
• Certificate III or Diploma in Early Childhood Education & Care (or ACECQA-approved equivalent)
• Proven 1-year minimum experience in long day care or similar setting.
• Demonstrated knowledge of EYLF and National Quality Standards
• Genuine passion for early childhood development with endless patience and creativity
• Current First Aid, Asthma & Anaphylaxis certificates as well as proof of vaccination
• Working with children rights
• Police check
• Strong communication skills to engage with children, colleagues and families
• References from previous employers

Why Apply?
This is more than a job - it's an opportunity to shape young lives in an environment that values educator wellbeing as much as child development. You'll receive:

• Above-award wages for qualified candidates
• Paid professional development opportunities
• Supportive leadership team with realistic expectations
• Purpose-built facilities with quality resources

If you're ready to make your mark in early childhood education with an organisation that values your expertise, we'd love to hear from you.

How to Apply:
Submit your resume and cover letter addressing your experience with the EYLF and your approach to play-based learning. Successful applicants will require valid working rights and must pass background checks.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Manager
Job Title: Registered Nurse (NEC)
Salary range: $80,000 - $90,000 depending on skill level and work experience + superannuation
Job Closure date: 30 days from day posted.

About the Role
Our client is seeking an experienced and compassionate Registered Nurse to join their dedicated aged care team. This is a pivotal role where you will have the opportunity to make a profound difference in the lives of residents, helping them to live with dignity, independence, and wellbeing.
You will be an integral part of a supportive and respectful community environment, dedicated to delivering exceptional person-centred care. Your primary responsibilities will include the provision of safe and high-quality clinical care, comprehensive medication management, and the ongoing monitoring of residents' health conditions. You will provide hands-on nursing support that is thoughtfully tailored to meet the individual needs and preferences of each resident.
Your commitment to fostering a homely and nurturing atmosphere will be key to ensuring every individual receives the best possible support to maintain their health, comfort, and overall quality of life. If this seems like a good fit, please read below!

Key Responsibilities

• Provide high-quality, person-centred nursing care to elderly residents, especially those with complex and changing health conditions.
• Deliver clinical care such as medication administration, wound care, chronic disease management and palliative care, in line with best practice.
• Assist residents and their families to make informed decisions about their care, ensuring their wishes and preferences are respected.
• Respond promptly and professionally to any changes in residents’ conditions and to clinical emergencies.
• Work closely with residents, families, and the multidisciplinary care team to assess care needs and develop individualized aged care plans.
• Review and update care plans regularly to reflect changing health status and personal goals.
• Ensure all nursing activities, progress notes and observations are clearly and accurately documented according to policy and legislative requirements.
• Supervise and mentor Enrolled Nurses, Personal Care Workers and other support staff to ensure safe, effective, and compassionate care delivery.
• Provide clear clinical direction and guidance, fostering a positive and collaborative team environment.
• Support staff to develop their knowledge and skills in aged care best practice.
• Maintain a safe, supportive and homelike environment that promotes residents’ health, comfort, security and quality of life.
• Uphold residents’ privacy, dignity, cultural identity and individual choices always.
• Comply with all relevant aged care standards, policies and procedures to ensure the highest levels of care quality and safety.
• Participate in continuous quality improvement initiatives to enhance the resident experience.
• Take part in ongoing training and professional development to keep up to date with aged care best practices, policies and regulatory requirements.
• Actively contribute to a positive workplace culture focused on learning, respect and excellence in care.

Skills & Experience
• Current registration with AHPRA as a Registered Nurse.
• Minimum 1 year of practical nursing experience, ideally in residential or community aged care.
• NDIS Worker Screening Check (current or dated within five years).
• Fully vaccinated for influenza (annually) and COVID-19.
• Demonstrated understanding of the Aged Care Quality Standards and person-centred care principles.
• Strong teamwork and leadership skills, with excellent communication and interpersonal abilities.
• Own reliable transport.
• Commitment to long-term employment in a caring, community-focused aged care setting.

Why Join Us?
Top-tier salary based on experience and skill level.
Premium facility and support provided.

Apply Now:
If you have a genuine passion for NEC Nursing and want to be part of a dedicated team making a positive impact in your community, we’d love to hear from you.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

result.description:
AMA 

AMA Group is the leader in collision repair, with the biggest network of facilities across Australia and New Zealand, supported by Australia’s leading distributor of vehicle parts and accessories. Our Team provides repairs for light to high-severity collisions — on everything from small private vehicles and prestige cars to commercial trucks and buses. With around 3,500 people across approximately 150 locations, we deliver outstanding customer service and get over 300,000 people and businesses back on the road every year. With AMA Group, you can go anywhere.

 

 CAPITAL SMART 

With over 50 repair centres across Australia and New Zealand, Capital S.M.A.R.T is the industry leader We are the pioneers of customer satisfaction and innovation standards, and pride ourselves on providing our employees with safe, supportive, and rewarding working conditions. With an extensive network across Australia and New Zealand, as part of our Team, you can go anywhere.

 

ACM PARTS

ACM Parts is Australia’s largest provider of alternative and specialty parts to the automotive repair industry, keeping vehicles on the road. We are reimaging the way vehicles can be repaired by providing a choice of options that suit their needs. We offer a comprehensive range of Reclaimed, Genuine, and Aftermarket parts as. ACM Parts is reinventing the quality and service standards of the repair industry. It’s our mission to re-define and repair.

 

The Opportunity
We have an exciting opportunity for Centre Manager at either of our AMA Group Solutions or Capital S.M.A.R.T Repairs team. This is a full time position. 

Reporting to the State Operations Manager, you will take ownership of this centre by providing leadership and motivation to your team whilst having a significant impact on the day to day operational running of the site. This permanent full-time role will be provide you with opportunities for growth, stability and security as part of the bigger AMA Group. 

Role responsibilities
Production Workshop Management: oversee production management of the workshop to ensure targets are achieved and vehicles are repaired to their pre-accident condition in accordance with AMA and Work Provider quality expectations.

Quality, Quotes, Parts and Vehicle Management: ensure comprehensive and accurate quotes, QA inspections and vehicles are repaired to their pre-accident condition. 
Customer Service and Stakeholder Management: provide exceptional customer service to all clients and work providers through prompt, professional and friendly interactions.
Profit and Loss, Reporting and Administration: ensure the site is operating profitability. Prepare and review P&Ls, Budgets, Job costings, KPIs, Management Reports by utilising the tools provided to understand site performance.
Leadership and People Management: oversee staffing on site and ensure staffing levels and processes are in place. Proactively build and maintain positive work provider relationships.
Work Health and Safety (WHS): ensure that the site remains safe by maintaining the WHS management system, all WHS policies and procedures are followed and safety incidences/near misses are immediately reported and actioned.
 

Benefits

Reward & recognition
Career development and training
Referral bonus for recommending a friend to work with us
Discounts on parts and tools
Uniforms
24/7 professional counselling for Team members and their immediate families
We champion our Team, because it’s our people that set us apart and drive our business' success. We focus on individual strengths and value differences to bring the best out of people, enhancing their skills and capabilities to build fulfilling careers. 

AMA Group is an equal opportunity employer. We are dedicated to finding the best fit for every role. All qualified applications will be considered regardless of gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, disability, or sexual orientation.

No matter who you are, if you have the drive and talent to progress, when you’re part of our Team, you’re going places - APPLY NOW.

result.description: Cox Purtell Most organisations either have an AI strategist who can't build, or a builder who has no seat at the table. This role offers a rare chance to stay close to the tech, while also having a seat at the table.  A large higher education organisation is bringing in a Head of AI Delivery to own applied AI end to end: shape where it goes, and build the systems that get it there. This is not a hands-off strategy seat, and it is not a pure build seat. It is both, deliberately.   What you'll own:  - Direct input into the organisation's AI roadmap and strategic digital plan - not just executing someone else's - End-to-end delivery of agentic AI, generative AI, LLM and RAG-based systems from concept to production - Establishing the AI capability function from scratch - tooling, delivery patterns, operating model - Mentoring and uplifting existing staff as you build the function around you - Governance, risk, and responsible AI as a core pillar, not an afterthought - transparency, bias mitigation, post-deployment monitoring - Enterprise architecture and cloud platform decisions (Azure, AWS, GCP) - Direct engagement with the CIO, COO, and senior executive leadership   Who you'll report to:  The CIO - technically astute, commercially savvy, and driven to produce outcomes. You'll also be visible to the COO and senior executive leadership. What you build gets seen, and it's expected to demonstrate real value within the first 3-6 months.   What you need:  - You've shipped AI or ML into production before, in a real enterprise - not just a lab or a pilot - You've built or led an AI capability function from the ground up - You've worked hands-on with agentic AI and multi-agent orchestration, not just read about it - RAG, prompt engineering, MLOps/LLMOps - you've actually done this work, not sat in on it - You take governance and responsible AI seriously, in a regulated or genuinely complex environment - You're comfortable being watched by executives and the board, not just your manager   The setup:  - Brisbane-based, hybrid - 2-3 days on-site - Contracted as 12-month fixed-term, but the engagement runs multi-year - real security, not a cliff-edge contract - $180,000-$220,000 plus superannuation - Relocation support available - Standard benefits including leave loading and salary packaging  One non-negotiable: you'll need Australian citizenship or permanent residency for this one.  You'll thrive here if you want both the seat at the table and your hands on the keyboard. You'll struggle here if you only want one or the other - this role won't let you pick.  Want the full brief?
